newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - Dlr/mark vols jump, dlr/yen off highs.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Dlr/mark vols jump, dlr/yen off highs.

text.p: Implied volatilities for dollar/mark options rose in thin trade, despite a range-bound spot market, while dollar/yen volatilities came off overnight highs as spot pulled back below 116 yen, traders said.

"From a technical perspective, it looks like a move is imminent (in spot dollar/mark)," said a trader at a U.S. bank in California, referring to a triangle pattern on the daily chart that has been forming since early December.
"Volatilities have definitely factored in that because implied volatilities are much higher than actual volatilities," he noted.
"People are looking for a corresponding move, either triggered by mark/yen perhaps, or some comment (from monetary authorities) in dollar/yen that would drive the crosses," he said.
One-month dollar/mark implied volatility stood at 8.5/8.7 percent, up over half a point from Friday's levels.

The dollar, after topping out near 1.5735 marks on December 3 and bottoming near 1.5280 on December 6, hase been narrowing in toward current levels in the upper-1.55-mark area, trading in the range of 1.5550-1.5600 for most of the past several days.

"This is a classic case of volatilities picking up because of the expectation of a future movement -- as opposed to all the months we spent this year pricing one-year volatility based on the last two hours of what spot was doing," said a trader at a European bank in Chicago.
In dollar/yen, where spot has become much more choppy in the past few sessions, implied volatilities slipped from overnight highs as the greenback pulled back below 116 yen.
"The 116 (yen) level remains the key at this point to maintain volatility advances," the California trader said.
One-month dollar/yen implied volatility eased to 9.0/9.2 percent by late U.S. morning, off about a quarter point from European highs touched when the dollar bobbed above 116 yen.
Traders said they were not keen on building fresh positions ahead of the New Year's Day holiday.
"At this level right now, there seems to be virtually no trade going on," the California trader said.

Risk reversals, which reflect pricing differential between puts and calls, for shorter maturities flipped in favor of yen puts for the first time in a few months in the absence of Japanese exporters, the perennial buyers of yen calls.

One-month dollar/yen risk reversal stood at 0.0/0.3 percent in favor of yen puts, compared with 0.2/0.4 percent in favor of yen calls on Friday. Beyond three- to four-months, risk reversals were still skewed for yen calls, however.

With the dollar rallying against the yen and dollar/mark lagging behind recently, mark/yen has risen sharply to the mid-74 yen area. One-month mark/yen volatilities were up nearly half a point from Friday at 8.1/8.4 percent.
